entries.bottom_line: The Democratic sweep of Congress has thrown the CLARITY Act's revival into serious doubt just as MSCI's final list of index-excluded Bitcoin treasury companies is due November 11, compounding capital-markets access risk for DAT/treasury equities heading into month-end.

updates.headline: Democrats sweep Congress, CLARITY Act outlook darkens
updates.what_happened: Democrats won control of both the Senate and House in the November 3 midterms, and analysts say this materially dims prospects for the stalled CLARITY Act crypto market-structure bill. Expected incoming Senate Banking Chair Elizabeth Warren and other Democrats are seen prioritizing scrutiny of Trump's personal crypto dealings over passing industry-friendly legislation, with one analyst saying the industry should "expect the Clarity Act to remain on hold through 2028."

updates.headline: Democrats weigh new, tougher crypto market-structure bill
updates.what_happened: House Democrats are reportedly discussing a broader crypto market-structure bill for the next Congress that could expand SEC authority over crypto markets while narrowing CFTC responsibilities, and could add restrictions on crypto-related activities by Trump and other federal officials. The new Congress convenes in January 2027, creating a different political environment for crypto regulation.

updates.headline: MSCI final Bitcoin-treasury index exclusion list due Nov 11
updates.what_happened: MSCI confirmed its finalized non-operating-company methodology will determine the final list of potentially excluded constituents (including Strategy and Metaplanet) on November 11, 2026, with index changes effective at the close of trading on November 30. A preliminary list already flags Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi for possible removal under the five-ratio financial screen, though two-year filing buffers limit immediate turnover.

updates.headline: FinCEN cuts exchange MEXC off from US financial system
updates.what_happened: Treasury's FinCEN designated MEXC Global a primary money-laundering concern on November 6, barring US financial institutions from processing transfers to or from the exchange over an alleged $16.7 billion in illicit flows tied to Russia, Iran and North Korea between 2021 and 2026. The order, issued under the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act, takes effect 30 days after Federal Register publication; MEXC said user assets remain secure and it is conducting an independent AML review.

updates.headline: Bank of Russia approves BTC, ETH, USDT for retail trading
updates.what_happened: The Bank of Russia approved Bitcoin, Ether and USDT as the first cryptocurrencies that non-qualified (retail) investors may buy through licensed brokers, asset managers and exchanges, effective November 17, 2026, with a 300,000-ruble annual purchase cap per intermediary. The Moscow Exchange is targeting a December 1 launch for Bitcoin and Ether trading.

updates.headline: Bitcoin, Ether ETFs post large joint weekly outflows
updates.what_happened: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly $1.3 billion in net outflows for the week ending November 7, the largest weekly outflow since late June 2026, while spot Ether ETFs also shed money rather than drawing inflows as in the prior reporting period. The outflows coincided with Bitcoin trading near three-month lows around $75,000-76,000 amid higher Treasury yields following a stronger-than-expected October jobs report.

entries.bottom_line: The Fed advanced GENIUS Act stablecoin capital/reserve rulemaking and the CFTC issued detailed crypto margin and capital-charge guidance, extending the post-CLARITY-Act regulatory-agency workaround while the MSCI treasury-index exclusion consultation heads toward its September 30 close.

updates.headline: Fed proposes GENIUS Act stablecoin reserve, capital rules
updates.what_happened: The Federal Reserve Board requested public comment on two proposals implementing its GENIUS Act supervisory role: the first would require Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuers to fully back tokens with permissible reserve assets such as short-term Treasury bills, plus standardized capital and risk-management requirements and custody rules; the second creates an application process for banks seeking to issue stablecoins through a subsidiary. Comments are due 60 days after Federal Register publication, ahead of the GENIUS Act's January 2027 effective date.

updates.headline: CFTC issues detailed crypto margin, capital-charge guidance
updates.what_happened: The CFTC's Market Participants Division, Division of Market Oversight, and Division of Clearing and Risk published updated FAQs allowing FCMs to accept customer non-security crypto (including stablecoins) as margin, and setting a 20 percent capital charge on proprietary bitcoin and ether positions aligned with SEC broker-dealer haircuts. The guidance also permits derivatives clearing organizations to accept crypto assets as initial margin for cleared transactions.

updates.headline: CFTC reviews $5B pattern in Kalshi ETH perpetuals
updates.what_happened: The CFTC is examining nearly one million trades on Kalshi's Ethereum perpetual futures market since August 2026, with over a third clustering around identical order sizes totaling more than $5 billion in volume. Kalshi denies wash-trading allegations, attributing the pattern to standard market-making activity.

updates.headline: MoonPay to acquire broker-dealer North Capital for tokenized securities
updates.what_happened: MoonPay plans to acquire private-market platform North Capital in an all-stock transaction valued at more than $60 million. North Capital holds SEC-related broker-dealer and ATS licenses and has supported billions in transaction volume, which would give MoonPay added regulatory capability for issuance, custody, and secondary trading of private and tokenized securities.

entries.bottom_line: The dominant sector-wide overhang remains MSCI's live consultation on excluding Bitcoin/digital-asset treasury companies from its Global Investable Market Indexes, with the comment window closing September 30 and results due October 16, 2026, while regulators continue advancing custody and market-structure rules in the wake of the stalled CLARITY Act.

updates.headline: MSCI index-exclusion consultation for Bitcoin treasuries nears close
updates.what_happened: MSCI's renewed consultation would classify certain 'non-operating' companies — explicitly naming Strategy and Metaplanet based on a May 2026 simulation, with uranium holder Yellow Cake also swept in — as ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes. Public feedback closes September 30, 2026, with results expected October 16, and any changes would take effect in the November 2026 index review, potentially forcing passive-fund selling.

updates.headline: SEC signals crypto custody rulemaking proceeding despite CLARITY stall
updates.what_happened: Following the Senate's failure to advance the CLARITY Act, SEC Chair Paul Atkins publicly reiterated that the agency will act on crypto market structure 'with or without legislation,' with a crypto custody rule proposal — sent to OMB in late August — cited as a near-term priority alongside continuing work on Regulation Crypto Assets.

entries.bottom_line: With the CLARITY Act stalled in the Senate, U.S. regulators (CFTC, SEC, OCC) are advancing crypto market-structure and capital-markets access piecemeal via existing authority, expanding derivatives products and stablecoin bank charters rather than waiting for comprehensive legislation.

updates.headline: CFTC broadens no-action relief for crypto wallet software
updates.what_happened: The CFTC's Market Participants Division issued Staff Letter 26-25, expanding a no-action position previously limited to Phantom Technologies to cover any qualifying 'passive software' provider (wallets, DeFi front ends, apps) that routes users to CFTC-registered derivatives venues without requiring introducing-broker registration. The relief lasts until the Commission finalizes formal rulemaking and does not shield providers from other laws such as money-transmission or DOJ criminal statutes.

updates.headline: Coinbase, Kalshi, Bitnomial file for single-stock perpetual futures
updates.what_happened: Coinbase Derivatives, Kalshi, and Kraken-linked Bitnomial each filed proposed rule changes with the SEC/CFTC on September 18 to list cash-settled, no-expiry perpetual futures on individual U.S. stocks and ETFs (Apple, Tesla, Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, SPY, QQQ among proposed underliers). CFTC approval remains pending for all three filings, and the products would give price exposure only, without ownership, dividend, or voting rights.

updates.headline: Bastion wins conditional OCC national trust bank charter
updates.what_happened: Stablecoin infrastructure provider Bastion received preliminary conditional OCC approval to convert its New York trust charter into a national trust bank charter (Bastion Platforms National Trust Company), covering GENIUS Act-compliant stablecoin custody, wallets, payment infrastructure, and white-label issuance. The charter bars deposit-taking and lending and is not FDIC-insured, joining Ripple, Circle, and BitGo among firms securing similar federal stablecoin charters.

entries.bottom_line: A failed Senate crypto market-structure vote and a surprise Fed rate hike to 3.75%-4.00% raised financing costs and regulatory uncertainty for treasury companies, even as the SEC and CFTC moved unilaterally to advance tokenization and crypto market-structure rules via executive authority.

updates.headline: Senate blocks CLARITY Act crypto market-structure bill
updates.what_happened: The Senate cloture vote on the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act failed 49-50, well short of the 60 votes needed to advance the bill, with three Republicans breaking ranks and Democratic negotiators who had worked on the bill all voting no. The failure stalls the first comprehensive federal crypto market-structure framework and pushes prospects for passage into 2027.

updates.headline: SEC issues Innovation Exemption for tokenized stock trading
updates.what_happened: The SEC issued a temporary, five-year conditional exemption allowing "Tokenized Securities Venues" (TSVs) to trade tokenized NMS stocks via permissioned automated market makers without registering as exchanges, and separately exempted qualifying liquidity providers from dealer registration. Chair Atkins framed the move as a direct response to the Senate's failure to pass crypto legislation, positioning the SEC to advance capital-markets modernization using existing statutory authority.

updates.headline: CFTC files crypto market-structure rulemaking with White House
updates.what_happened: Two days after the CLARITY Act failure, the CFTC submitted a prerule filing (RIN 3038-AF80, "Regulation of Crypto Asset Transactions and Crypto Asset Markets") to the White House OIRA, invoking Dodd-Frank authority to create a new registration category for crypto trading venues without new legislation. Chairman Selig said the agency is "locked in and ready to ship" rules, though the process could take until late 2027 to become final and binding.

updates.headline: Fed raises rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%, first hike since 2023
updates.what_happened: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75%-4.00%, its first increase in over three years, with updated projections pointing to a possible further hike this year. The decision, driven by elevated inflation and Middle East tension, raises financing and carry costs for leveraged treasury-company balance sheets.

updates.headline: Bitcoin ETFs post $463M outflows, Ether ETFs draw $197M inflows
updates.what_happened: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $462.7 million in net outflows for the week of Sept 8-11, ending a three-week inflow streak, led by ARK 21Shares and Grayscale redemptions, while spot Ether ETFs reversed course with $196.9 million in net inflows, led by BlackRock's ETHA. The divergence suggests institutional rotation between the two largest crypto assets rather than a broad sector exit.

updates.headline: Bitcoin treasury sector market value down sharply from peak
updates.what_happened: Reports citing sector trackers indicate the roughly 179 listed Bitcoin treasury companies have collectively lost tens of billions of dollars in market value since mid-2025, with commentators flagging tightening financing conditions and rising investor scrutiny of the model's sustainability as the number of competing issuers has grown.
